claims.text: The proposed intervention is an active-learning machine-learning interatomic potential coupled to enhanced free-energy sampling.
The surrogate potential would be trained using sparse ab initio molecular-dynamics data.
Enhanced sampling would use umbrella sampling or thermodynamic integration along an optimized reaction coordinate.
On-the-fly ab initio corrections would be used during free-energy sampling.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can approach underlying DFT accuracy in multicomponent alloys.
The proposed surrogate can reproduce the solid- and fluid-phase free-energy landscape.
The surrogate can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling in both solid and fluid phases.
Iteratively adding training configurations from phase-transition-critical regions will improve reproduction of the relevant free-energy landscape.
Restricting expensive ab initio evaluations to regions of elevated model uncertainty will reduce computational cost while efficiently sampling the relevant configuration space.
Regions near phase transitions or involving strong anharmonic interactions will exhibit elevated surrogate-model uncertainty.
The method will reduce computational cost by approximately one order of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The method will predict solid–fluid free-energy differences within a few meV per atom, ideally less than 5 meV per atom, of full ab initio molecular dynamics.
The method will outperform TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The method is applicable near and above melting temperatures.
The method is applicable across elemental, binary, and multicomponent high-entropy alloy composition spaces.
Extreme compositions or temperatures far from the trained phase boundaries may reduce reliability.
Full ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD explicitly retain all relevant entropy contributions.
Full ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD have very high computational costs, particularly for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
A deviation greater than 5 meV per atom from full ab initio molecular-dynamics phase free energies would falsify the hypothesis.
